method.identity: oldA/oldB use one native Module object; newA/newB use another. All labels use identical options, full default trace, generated CPU bytes and ABI. Fresh instances and memories for every run.
method.compilation: CPU lowering happens once per case; the unmodified precompiled loader creates a fresh CPU Module on each construction, asserted by object identity. Construction/compilation, input setup, snapshots, hashing and checks are outside execution timers.
method.warmup: Each label receives the same number of discarded full-workload warmups in recorded Williams order (position-balanced when warmups is4 or8). Warmups are retained and checked against the same exact reference; no stable-tiering guarantee is inferred.
method.order: Williams four-label design and reversed rows; every label occupies every position equally and every directed adjacent pair occurs equally often. Runs are serial. No affinity, GC or CPU-frequency control.
method.comparison: Exact PCM bytes, all CPU/device state and diagnostics, SRAM/Flash/EEPROM/IRQ and complete host tail after every batch. No observer omission or diagnostic normalization.
method.interpretation: oldA/oldB and newA/newB are null controls. Cross-version ratio is geometric mean of the two old elapsed times divided by geometric mean of the two new times within each trial. This is coupled Node execution; it does not isolate exclusive subsystem costs or prove a C-source cause.
